<section>
<h3>Why Extreme Value Distributions?</h3>

<div class="image-box3">
<img src="images/exponential_fit_failure_display.png" style="display: block; margin: 0 auto; width: 70%;">
</div>

</section>

<section>
<h3>How do you Model Distributions' <em>Tails</em>?</h3>

<h2 style="text-align: center; color: forestgreen">GPD Distribution Style</h2>

Daily precipitation $\rightarrow$ random variable $X$; 

Exceedance threshold $u$; 

Exceedance daily precipitations $\rightarrow$ $Y = X - u | X > u$.


Using Extreme Value Theory, the distribution of the *exceedances* can be modeled approximately by some special distributions. One is the Generalized Pareto Distribution:

$$
P(Y \lt y | X > u) \sim GPD(\mu, \sigma, \xi)
$$

</section>

<section>
<h3>Getting a GPD Distribution Fit</h3>

$$
\text{GPD}(\mu, \sigma, \xi) \sim F(y) = 
\begin{cases}
1 - \left(1 + \xi \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma} \right)^{\frac{-1}{\xi}} \text{for } \xi \neq 0, \\
1 - \exp(-\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}) \text{ for } \xi = 0,
\end{cases}
$$

Given $x \ge \mu$ if $\xi \ge 0$. 

We will turn to MLE to estimate $\sigma$ and $\xi$. We will minimize the negative log-likelihood function $\ell(\sigma, \xi) = -n \ln\sigma - \left(\frac{1}{\xi}+1 \right) \sum_i^{260} \ln \left(1 + \xi\frac{x_i-\mu}{\sigma}\right),$ given that $\mu = Q_{0.99} = 44.7 \text{ mm }  = 1.75 \text{ inches}$
</section>

<section>
<h3>How do you Model Distributions' <em>Tails</em>?</h3>

<h2 style="text-align: center; color: forestgreen">GEV Distribution Style</h2>

</section>

<section>
<h3>Getting a GEV Distribution Fit</h3>

Again, we'll use MLE to estimate $\mu_{GEV}$, $\sigma_{GEV}$, and $\xi_{GEV}$, minimizing the negative log-likelihood function. 

</section>
